risk_note: RV2 (apps/api/src/modules/platform/**, payment, union). FU-KMS-ADAPTER (orchestrator 11-02 03:49, plan accepted 04:12). A KeyProvider over Aliyun KMS for both field keyrings, and KMS secrets for the two collection channels and the Pinduoduo, Taobao, Jingdong and Dataoke credentials, prod only for the secrets. New variables KMS_REGION_ID, KMS_ENDPOINT, KMS_KEY_ID, KMS_RAM_ROLE (local / test refuse them) and PAY_ALIPAY_KEY_MODE. Credentials are the ECS RAM role over IMDSv2, no static AccessKey; the SDK loads only when KMS is configured. Without KMS_* behaviour is unchanged and no frozen test was edited. Configured but unreadable fails closed: keyrings and union adapters refuse to start, a channel answers kms_unavailable and never falls back to a fake one (D10-554). One addition beyond the brief: the prior identity keyring's refusal to share a data key with the main keyring now also runs when the main keyring is under KMS (unit test AC-B1-30a-U#3); it would otherwise have been skipped in prod. Only exercised against an SDK stub: no real KMS connection, which needs the owner to open KMS. The real SDK is only checked to load and build a client without sending anything.

reviews.note: round 1 (couli-runs/B1-30a/review-codex.json), no in-scope findings, static, no tests run and no real KMS. out_of_scope holds one S1: BR-PAY-08 ① and 规划/02 §12.6 say only api's payment module reads collection keys, while ruling D10-549 and this code allow api, worker and admin; raised to the orchestrator, refs of this task are empty. A unit test of the endpoint check was added after the review; no implementation change.

spec_test_review.note: fresh Claude, round 1 pass with 3 S2, covered outside the frozen rule tests: wrong key slot wiring by implementer unit test AC-B1-30a-U#4; endpoint characters before the suffix by the strict host pattern and AC-B1-30a-U#5; a static credentials import by construction, sdk.ts is the only importer and loads it dynamically, no test pins it. After r1, CI gitleaks (rule cn-doc-secret) flagged three synthetic constants in the rule tests; a new independent Claude renamed them and gave them low-entropy values. The diff against the reviewed rule tests is only those renames and values (checked by the implementer), red re-run passed 132, not reviewed again.
